subject: Urgent: CheckoutCo streaming handshake degradation — parser edge-case causing latency & 5xxs
messages:

Cc: ops@checkoutco.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Live checkout stalls and 5xxs during 08:00-09:00 PT — urgent

Markus —

We started seeing severe issues during peak this morning (08:15–08:55 PT): checkout requests experience 3–10s latencies and intermittent 502/504 errors. Error rate spiked to ~12% on the payments path. This is directly impacting order completion and revenue.

Attached is a small sample of our telemetry (checkoutco_metrics_0915.csv). We are using Redwood's client SDK v1.4.1 (beta) with streaming turned on for live receipts. We rolled back to non-streaming on one zone and saw immediate improvement — but we need a stable fix, not a manual workaround.

Can we get an urgent triage and an ETA for a mitigation? We're available for a call now if needed.

— Sophie

Sophie@checkoutco.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Live checkout stalls — initial triage

Markus / team — initial findings:

- Observed pattern: client connections that use streaming show repeated parser-state errors on our ingress (parser_error: unexpected_trailer_start). This correlates with spikes in retry traffic and CPU jitter in the streaming workers.
- Impact window: 08:12–08:58 PT (matches customer). Error rate on that pool rose from 0.6% -> 11.8%.
- Repro: limited repro with CheckoutCo's payloads + proxy chain — when an upstream proxy re-chunks a chunked transfer, our streaming parser occasionally treats a trailer fragment as a new header block, leaving the parser in a busy loop and triggering connection resets.

Quick mitigations we can execute now (low risk):
1) Flip routing for CheckoutCo to non-streaming endpoint (route flag: streaming_enabled=false) — roll forward to landing zone B. This is what Sophie tried; we can script and automate it across regions (5–10 min per region).
2) Apply ingress timeout tuning to break parser-stuck connections after 400ms of no-header progress.
3) Push SDK downgrade recommendation to CheckoutCo (v1.3.8 stable) while we patch.

Longer-term fix: safe header reassembly + trailer-ignore heuristics in parser. Grace, can you own a PR for that?

Attachments: short log sample pasted below:
[edge] 2026-09-15T08:21:12.412Z parser_error unexpected_trailer_start stream_id=54321 conn=10.2.3.45
[edge] 2026-09-15T08:21:12.418Z conn_reset reason=parser_backoff stream_id=54321
[edge] 2026-09-15T08:21:12.421Z retry_from_client client_id=checkoutco-zoneA count=2

-Sean
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.g@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: naomi@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Live checkout stalls — root cause and patch plan

Sean / Markus — deep dive update after running local repro + trace: root cause summary:

- Root cause: parser state machine did not correctly handle fragmented trailer frames when an intermediate proxy split chunked transfer encodings across TCP segments. In certain fragment boundary alignments, the parser interprets the initial trailer bytes as the start of a new header block and stalls while waiting for a colon-delimited header (never arrives). This leaves tokens queued and pushes worker threads into backpressure -> retries.
- Why it surfaced now: CheckoutCo upgraded to SDK v1.4.1 which sets aggressive keepalives and uses a new buffered-write path that increases the likelihood of upstream re-chunking at the proxy layer. The combination exposed an untested parser state transition.

Proposed remediation plan (ordered):
A) Immediate (hours): roll customer routing to non-streaming endpoint (Sean to run toggle script). Notify customer and confirm improvement.
B) Hotfix (24–48h): server-side parser patch that: (1) reassembles headers across small trailer fragments up to 256 bytes, (2) adds a conservative safety timeout to abandon malformed header-state after 250ms and return a clear 499/400 instead of looping, and (3) adds telemetry counters for "trailer-as-header" occurrences. Patch PR: https://redwood.internal/pr/4781 (hotfix branch: parser-hotfix/1.4.2). Attached diff: hotfix_header_reassembly_1_4_2.diff
C) SDK guidance (48–72h): publish advisory for v1.4.1 callers to either downgrade or enable fallback-mode: streaming_send_mode=legacy until we ship SDK v1.4.2 with tighter write coalescing.

Canary plan: run patch in one US zone (us-west-2b) for 30m with traffic mirroring; monitor p99 latency, error-rate, and parser counter. If green, roll to rest of US regions.

I'll open the PR and queue CI. ETA for PR -> canary: ~12–18h (depends on warmup).

-Grace

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>

Team — thanks for the quick triage. Sophie, appreciate the details and the telemetry sample.

Customer impact summary (for execs): ~15% of orders during the peak window failed to complete in affected zones. CheckoutCo has temporarily routed traffic away from streaming endpoint and is observing initial improvements. They are asking for:
- A clear ETA for a permanent fix (they want 48h max)
- A small credit for the outage window
- A short incident note we can share internally and with CheckoutCo tomorrow morning (07:30 PT)

Immediate asks for eng: please prioritize the hotfix PR and the canary automation. Sean — please provide the routing toggle script and steps so I can run it if needed during the call with the customer at 10:00 PT.

I'll draft the customer-facing note (copy below) and share for sign-off.

Customer note (draft):
"Sophie — we've identified an edge-case in our streaming parser that can cause elevated latencies and connection resets when certain proxy re-chunking patterns occur. We've implemented a routing mitigation for your account and are deploying a targeted hotfix across a canary zone. We'll update you with a firm ETA within 12 hours."

-Naomi

Subject: Escalation summary — CheckoutCo streaming handshake degradation (action required)

Execs — brief summary and requested leadership actions:

Summary: On 2026-09-15 CheckoutCo experienced a latency spike and increased 5xx rate (~12%) during the morning peak in multiple US zones. Root cause traced to an edge-case in our streaming parser that is triggered by header/trailer fragmentation from upstream proxies when clients use SDK v1.4.1 with aggressive keepalive/coalescing. Customer mitigated by routing to non-streaming endpoint; customer impact was limited but revenue-affecting.

Actions completed by the team:
- Routing fallback executed for CheckoutCo (Naomi/Sean) — immediate improvement confirmed.
- Hotfix PR opened (Grace) — parser reassembly + timeout. PR: https://redwood.internal/pr/4781
- Canary plan prepared for us-west-2b; canary instrumentation added.

Requested from leadership:
1) Approve 24–48h engineering escalation (swap engineering capacity from lower-priority items to finish hotfix validation and canary rollout).
2) Approve a customer credit of one day of committed usage for CheckoutCo (rough estimate until further calculation by finance).
3) Support for a public-facing incident note and a controlled postmortem distribution (we plan to include remediation steps and SDK guidance).

Proposed timeline: hotfix -> canary start by EOD (US) today; full roll within 48 hours if canary is green. Will keep you posted every 6 hours while active.

-Markus
